correctness.rationale: Along a successful sequence every forced color is required in every proper extension, so a successful seed has one proper completion and counting its restrictions does not duplicate it. Two blank peripheral vertices in the same petal cannot be first among that pair to color, even if the hub is colored. A colored hub therefore allows any pattern of at most one peripheral blank per petal. A blank hub must be first to color, because each blank peripheral has at most m-2 visible neighbors before it. Within restrictions of a fixed completion this is possible exactly when all m-1 non-hub colors are visible somewhere, excluding exactly m-1 patterns, each with one peripheral blank of the same color in every petal. Multiplying by A=m((m-1)!)^k gives the stated B, and weighting each term by p^(N-j)(1-mp)^j yields FC, including the endpoints as a polynomial identity. The top coefficient A[(m-1)^k-(m-1)] is positive for k>=2 and m>=3; its cancellation at k=1 agrees with the complete-graph boundary. A separate finite reverse-step enumeration from a fixed proper completion (/workspace/branches/replay/r2_reverse.py) matched coefficients for seven pairs, including k=3,m=4 and k=2,m=5. That check corroborates the proof and does not extend it to excess palettes.
